name: Bauernschnapsen
description: Bauernschnapsen (Viererschnapsen) is the premier four-player partnership variant of the Austrian national game Schnapsen. Played with a stripped 20-card deck, it combines the intense card-point counting of the original game with complex partnership bidding and higher stakes. Each round is a battle to reach 66 points through tricks and marriages, while the overall session is a race to reach 24 game points. Famous for its 'Stechzwang' (trump compulsion) and various special contracts like 'Gang' and 'Bauern', it is a cornerstone of Central European tavern culture.

overview.description: Bauernschnapsen (Viererschnapsen) is the premier four-player partnership variant of the Austrian national game Schnapsen. Played with a stripped 20-card deck, it combines the intense card-point counting of the original game with complex partnership bidding and higher stakes. Each round is a battle to reach 66 points through tricks and marriages, while the overall session is a race to reach 24 game points. Famous for its 'Stechzwang' (trump compulsion) and various special contracts like 'Gang' and 'Bauern', it is a cornerstone of Central European tavern culture.

history.origins: Originating in Austria as an evolution of 2-player Schnapsen (and the earlier 66), Bauernschnapsen adapted the 'short deck' mechanics to a four-player format. It emerged as a distinct social tradition in Austrian rural communities ('Bauern' meaning farmers) where partnership play was preferred for social gatherings.
timeline: 18th Century: Early 'Sixty-Six' games spread across the Habsburg Empire.
19th Century: Schnapsen stabilizes as the primary Austrian variant.
Early 20th Century: Bauernschnapsen (Viererschnapsen) becomes the standardized partnership format in Alpine regions.
Present: One of Austria's most popular card games, with dedicated tournaments and regional clubs.
history.cultural: Regarded as a test of mental arithmetic and partnership intuition. It is a staple of 'Wirtshaus' (tavern) culture in Austria, Bavaria, and South Tyrol.
history.evolution: The game evolved from a simple point-race into a complex bidding game where the value of game points depends on the margin of victory (Schneider/Schwarz).

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships; partners sit opposite each other.
setup.deck: 20 cards. Ranks: Ace (11), 10 (10), King (4), Queen (Ober, 3), Jack (Unter, 2) in four suits.
setup.dealing: Dealer deals 3 cards to each player. Forehand (left of dealer) calls trump or knocks. Then 2 more cards are dealt to each player.
setup.equipment: Standard 20-card deck (French or German suited), score sheet.

rules.objective: Score 66 points in a deal to win the round, or satisfy a higher bid contract. First team to reach 24 game points (counting down) wins the session.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Bidding**: Forehand determines trump or everyone bids for special contracts. 2. **Marriages**: King and Queen of the same suit score bonus points (40 for trump, 20 for others) when one is led. 3. **Tricks**: Players must follow suit. If unable to follow suit, players MUST play a trump (Stechzwang). 4. **Counting**: Ace=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2. Total in deck is 120 points.
keyRules: Must trump if void in the led suit (Stechzwang).
Winning the last trick scores no extra points, but provides the final tally.
If a team reaches 66 points, they stop the game immediately.

strategy.basic: Count your points! Every card matters in a 20-card deck. Know when you have reached 66 so you can stop the hand before your opponents gain more points.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Volle' Strategy: Focus on capturing the Tens and Aces (the Volle). In a stripped deck, these 10/11 point cards are the difference between victory and defeat.
strategy.advanced: Bidding Precision: Understanding when to bid 'Gang' (winning all 5 tricks) vs 'Normal' requires perfect reading of the distribution based on the 3-card initial deal.
tips: A marriage declaration is often more valuable than a high-point capture.
Lead trumps early if you have a marriage to prevent opponents from trumping your King/Queen lead.

variations.name: Bettel
variations.description: A negative contract where the goal is to take no tricks at all.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Bettel uses the same core engine with contract-specific scoring changes that are not yet represented as structured overrides.

scoring.description: Points are tallied from tricks and marriages. The team reaching 66 points first wins the hand.
scoring.winCondition: The first team to reach 24 game points (counting down) or satisfy the declared contract.

synthesis.shortDescription: Experience the intense Austrian tradition of Bauernschnapsen. With only 20 cards in play, every card counts as you and your partner bid for high-stakes contracts. Navigate the rigid trump hierarchy and use strategic marriages to reach 66 points before your rivals can stop you.
